overall: Atlanta is warming steadily as of 10:20 ET, with the running max sitting at 84.2°F and a healthy warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr. The high dewpoint of 69.8°F signals significant atmospheric moisture, while light winds (5.8 mph) suggest limited boundary layer mixing to cap surface heating. Peak heating hours (roughly 2–4 PM ET) are still several hours away, and the current trajectory is consistent with a run into the lower-to-mid 90s.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful spread: GFS and HRRR are tightly clustered at 93.3°F, while ECMWF comes in at 91.8°F and the more conservative NBM at 91.1°F — a ~2.2°F range. max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence leans toward the low-to-mid 90s: GFS and HRRR both anchored at 93.3°F, the high-confidence Odd ensemble signal at 93–94°F, and a current warming rate that extrapolates comfortably into that range with peak heating still ahead. However, the conservative pull from NBM (91.1°F), ECMWF (91.8°F), and the Tier 4 Even model introduces enough uncertainty to shade the estimate slightly below 93°F. Best estimate is approximately 92.5°F, with moderate-to-good confidence given the GFS/HRRR/Odd model alignment but acknowledging the model spread and divergent ensemble signals.
